title: $Rf_*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes ($\ell$-adic and $\ell$-torsion $\Lambda$)
statement:
Let $\ell$ be the prime of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], invertible in $k$, and let $\Lambda$ be one of the
following commutative condensed rings ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]):

- $\underline E$ for a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$;
- $\underline{\cO}_E$ for a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, where $\cO_E$ is the ring of integers either of a
  subfield $E\subseteq\Qlb$ (with the topology restricted from $\Qlb$) or of a finite normed extension $E$ of
  $\mathbf Q_\ell$, given as its closed unit ball $\{x\in E:|x|\le1\}$;
- $\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]);
- $\underline T$ for a finite discrete ring $T$ with $\ell^nT=0$ for some $n\ge0$.

Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of the setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ is
bounded constructible ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is $Rf_*K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$
([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]). For a general $\Lambda$ this fails: for the constant discrete ring
$\mathbf F_p$, $p$ the characteristic of $k$, and $f\colon\mathbf A^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k$
algebraically closed, the Artin--Schreier sequence gives $H^1(\mathbf A^1,\mathbf F_p)=k[t]/(F-1)k[t]$, which is
infinite.

proof.text: Finite type over Spec k makes Y locally noetherian, and quasi-compactness of its structure map makes Y compact. Hence Y is noetherian. For a finiteness coefficient, bounded constructible Lambda_Y complexes form an isomorphism-closed triangulated subcategory. Its inverse image under the triangulated functor Rf_* is also isomorphism-closed and triangulated.

Apply finite truncation devissage to this inverse-image property. It suffices to show that it contains F[0] for every constructible Lambda_X module F. The right-derived functor lower-bound theorem puts Rf_*(F[0]) in degrees >=0. The single-sheaf upper-bound lemma supplies b with degrees <=b, and the separate single-sheaf constructibility lemma supplies constructible H^q for every q. Pair these data to get bounded constructibility of the single-sheaf image. Devissage then proves the assertion for K using hK.1 and hK.2.

proof_origin.place: Coefficient reductions are isolated on single sheaves; the source theorem is proved by the existing finite truncation induction and generic right-derived lower bound. Integral completion, rationalization and finite-stage descent remain in the two single-sheaf nodes.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be one of the $\ell$-adic condensed rings $\underline{\cO}_E$, $\underline E$
($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite; [det-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) or $\underline{\Qlb}$
([det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]), and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of the setting of
[sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ is bounded constructible
([det-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is $Rf_*K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$
([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]).

proof.text:
This is Deligne's finiteness theorem for $Rf_*$ (SGA 4½, *Th. finitude*, 1.1), extended to
$\ell$-adic coefficients through the integral route. Let first $\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E$ with
uniformizer $\pi_E$. By [sk-prop-integral-criterion], a complex $K$ is bounded constructible if
and only if it is derived complete and its reduction
$K_1=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_{E,X}}\cO_{E,X}/\pi_E$ is a bounded constructible complex pulled
back from the étale site. Now $Rf_*$ commutes with $\operatorname{R\lim}$, being a right adjoint,
and with cones, so it preserves derived completeness. It commutes with reduction modulo $\pi_E$,
because $K_1$ is the cone of multiplication by $\pi_E$ on $K$ and $Rf_*$ is exact. Since $K_1$
comes from the étale site, its pro-étale direct image is the pullback of its étale direct image
(\stacks{09A6}). Since $\ell$ is invertible on the finite type $k$-schemes $X$ and $Y$,
Deligne's theorem shows that this étale direct image is bounded with constructible cohomology.
Hence $Rf_*K$ is bounded constructible, by [sk-prop-integral-criterion] again.

For $\Lambda=\underline E$ and $\Lambda=\underline{\Qlb}$ it suffices to treat the generators of
[sk-lem-integral-models] (4): $Rf_*$ is exact and $\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$ is triangulated
([sk-cor-coefficient-heart-ii]). These generators come from objects $a_!L_0$ of
$\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ by inverting $\ell$ and, for $\Qlb$, by the filtered colimit over finite
extensions of $E$. Both are colimits of systems with a common lower bound, so $Rf_*$ commutes
with them by [sk-cor-pe-bounded-continuity] ($X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated). By the
integral case, $Rf_*$ maps the generators into $\Dbc(Y,E)$, respectively $\Dbc(Y,\Qlb)$.
